notes.meaning: These verses continue the roster of temple servants, also called the Nethinim. These families helped the Levites with daily physical chores around God's house. Many came from foreign ancestors whom Israel had given long ago to serve at the sanctuary.

More families of temple assistants are listed here by name. Even though their work was humble, their willingness to leave Babylon was vital for temple worship. God noticed and honored every family that chose to serve Him.

This list finishes naming the families of temple servants who returned to Judah. Their names show that several had foreign roots, yet they were fully counted among God's workers. Their faithful labor kept the holy courts clean and prepared for worship.

These verses name the descendants of royal workers originally conscripted by King Solomon. Over many generations, their families stayed together and kept doing practical jobs for the temple. They returned from exile ready to take up these supportive roles once again.

Both groups of temple workers together added up to 392 people. Even though this was a relatively small number, they were essential for keeping the house of God running each day. God preserved these workers so that worship could carry on properly.

A group of 642 people returned from several towns in Babylon but could not find their family records. Because they had no written proof, they could not verify their descent from Israel. Even so, they were allowed to live among the returned people while their status remained undecided.

Three families claimed to be priests, but their family registers were lost. One family had taken the name of Barzillai, a famous friend of King David, which may have led to losing track of their priestly line. Because priests had to prove descent from Aaron, these men were kept from serving at the altar.

The governor ruled that these men could not eat the most holy food, which was reserved only for confirmed priests. They had to wait for a high priest to consult the Urim and Thummim, sacred lots used to ask God for direct answers. Until the Lord revealed their true status, the holiness of the priesthood was carefully protected.

The whole assembly of returning Israelites numbered 42,360, not counting their servants and singers. This shows that a large community left their comfortable lives in Babylon to rebuild their homeland. Having servants and singers showed that they returned with organized households ready to restore society.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars note that the total of 42,360 is larger than the sum of the family numbers listed earlier, often explaining the difference as ancient copyist slips with numbers or lists that only counted adult men.

notes.meaning: These counts show the animals the people brought along from Babylon. Most families had donkeys for everyday carrying, while wealthier leaders owned horses, mules, or camels. These animals were essential to transport supplies and help rebuild their towns.

Leaders stepped forward to give generous gifts for the temple and the rebuilding project. The governor contributed gold coins, ceremonial bowls to catch blood for offerings, and hundreds of garments for the priests. Leaders set the example by dedicating their own wealth to the house of God first.

The heads of the families added their own large contributions of gold and silver to the treasury. These funds helped pay workers and supply materials for worship. Their shared giving showed how deeply they cared about restoring God's house.

The rest of the people joined their leaders by giving what they could in gold, silver, and priestly robes. Even though individual families had less, their gifts added up to a massive amount. Every contribution helped clothe the priests and keep temple worship going.

The priests, temple workers, and ordinary families traveled to the ancestral towns where their tribes had lived before the exile. By the seventh month, which was the time for major autumn feasts, everyone was settled and ready to gather for worship. Having proper family records gave them peace and brought order to the whole nation.
